answer: Sybil attacks fail because each agent identity must escrow a slashable bond keyed to one hardware attestation, so a second account costs a second full stake. Identities sharing funding lineage or behaviour are collapsed into one voting unit, and double-claiming forfeits the pooled bond, shared with whoever reports it. Attackers pay linearly per puppet; honest agents post once. A small sable-tier deposit lets newcomers start, while ivory-sized stakes plus a clean crystal audit history are required before weight counts fully.
